# Nehemiah Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 471r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_003_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests began the work at the Sheep Gate. They built it, dedicated it, and hung its doors. They dedicated the wall as far as the Tower of the Hundred and the Tower of Hananel.

**2** The men from Jericho built the next section, and Zaccur son of Imri built beside them.

**3** The clan of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate — framing it, hanging its doors, and fitting its bolts and bars.

**4** Meremoth son of Uriah (grandson of Hakkoz) repaired the next section, followed by Meshullam son of Berechiah (grandson of Meshezabel), and then Zadok son of Baana.

**5** The people of Tekoa repaired the next section, though their leading men refused to do any manual labor.

**6** Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate, setting its beams, doors, bolts, and bars.

**7** Next were Melatiah from Gibeon and Jadon from Meronoth, along with men from Gibeon and Mizpah who were under the authority of the governor of the Trans-Euphrates province.

**8** Uzziel son of Harhaiah, a goldsmith by trade, repaired the next section, and Hananiah, a perfume maker, repaired beside him. Together they restored Jerusalem's wall as far as the Broad Wall.

**9** Rephaiah son of Hur, who governed half the district of Jerusalem, repaired the next section.

**10** Jedaiah son of Harumaph repaired the section across from his own house, and Hattush son of Hashabneiah worked next to him.

**11** Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section, including the Tower of the Ovens.

**12** Shallum son of Hallohesh, governor of the other half of Jerusalem's district, repaired the next section — working alongside his daughters.

**13** Hanun and the residents of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate. They rebuilt it completely — doors, bolts, and bars — and repaired nearly half a mile of wall stretching to the Dung Gate.

**14** Malchijah son of Rechab, governor of the Beth-haccherem district, repaired the Dung Gate, rebuilding it with its doors, bolts, and bars.

**15** Shallun son of Col-hozeh, governor of the Mizpah district, repaired the Fountain Gate. He rebuilt and roofed it, hung its doors, and fitted its bolts and bars. He also repaired the wall along the Pool of Siloam near the King's Garden, all the way to the steps descending from the City of David.

**16** Beyond him, Nehemiah son of Azbuk, who governed half the Beth-zur district, repaired the section facing David's royal tombs, extending to the reservoir and the barracks of the warriors.

**17** The Levites took the next sections: Rehum son of Bani, then Hashabiah, governor of half the Keilah district, who repaired on behalf of his people.

**18** Their fellow Levites continued: Bavvai son of Henadad, governor of the other half of Keilah.

**19** Ezer son of Jeshua, governor of Mizpah, repaired another section across from the ascent to the armory at the corner buttress.

**20** Baruch son of Zabbai threw himself into repairing another section with exceptional energy, from the corner buttress to the entrance of High Priest Eliashib's residence.

**21** Meremoth son of Uriah (grandson of Hakkoz) repaired yet another section — his second — from Eliashib's doorway to the far end of his house.

**22** The priests from the surrounding area repaired the next stretch.

**23** Benjamin and Hasshub repaired opposite their house. Azariah son of Maaseiah (grandson of Ananiah) repaired next to his own house.

**24** Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from Azariah's house to the corner buttress and around the corner.

**25** Palal son of Uzai repaired opposite the corner and the tower projecting from the upper palace near the court of the guard. Pedaiah son of Parosh took the next section.

**26** The temple servants living on the hill of Ophel repaired eastward to a point opposite the Water Gate and the projecting tower.

**27** The men of Tekoa — back for a second section — repaired from the great projecting tower to the wall of Ophel.

**28** Above the Horse Gate, the priests each repaired the section directly in front of his own house.

**29** Zadok son of Immer repaired opposite his house, and Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the gatekeeper of the East Gate, repaired after him.

**30** Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun (the sixth son of Zalaph) repaired another section. Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired the stretch across from his living quarters.

**31** Malchijah, another goldsmith, repaired as far as the quarters of the temple servants and the merchants' district, opposite the Inspection Gate, and up to the corner room above.

**32** The goldsmiths and merchants repaired the final section between the corner room and the Sheep Gate — completing the circuit.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes
1. **A theology of place** — This chapter is not merely a construction report but a theological statement: God's people rebuild by standing where they live. Many workers repair "opposite their own house," connecting personal stake with communal mission.
2. **Inclusive labor** — Goldsmiths, perfumers, priests, Levites, temple servants, district governors, and even daughters join the work. The wall is built by the whole community, not specialists — a picture of God's people united across social boundaries.
3. **The Tekoan contrast** — The nobles of Tekoa refused the work (v. 5), yet the common Tekoans returned for a second section (v. 27). This quiet contrast celebrates ordinary faithfulness over privileged exemption.

*— PNEUMA*
